page: OVHcloud c3-64 is a compute-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, with one thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a local 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a Passmark CPU score of 63,662.12 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 18,263.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Memory performance is particularly notable, with a Passmark memory score in the top 10% and cached read-only small block memory bandwidth reaching 4,755.88 GB/sec. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression at 433.64 GB/sec and software compilation with Clang at 45,546.0, also rank in the top 25%. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,914.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 29.15 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance offers high resource density for compute-heavy workloads. It performs strongly in database operations, executing 77.38 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 31,841.07 on Passmark database tests. It is also capable of handling small-scale LLM inference, processing 2,858.15 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model, though performance drops to an average tier for 7B models. The server is well-suited for software compilation, database hosting, multi-threaded data processing, and ray tracing workloads.
